change_note: First themes for the Theme hunter: Space, AI, Chips, Software and Energy.
how_to_read: Our own short reading of how much competition each company has: dominant (one clear leader), few rivals, or crowded. A starting point to read further, not a fact and not advice.

themes.name: Space
themes.why: Rockets, satellites and internet from space. A young industry: a few winners can grow many times over, and many small companies fail.

companies.note: Launches most of the world's satellites and runs the biggest internet satellite network (Starlink).
The busiest US launcher after SpaceX, and it builds satellites too. A bigger rocket (Neutron) is its next step.
Satellites that talk straight to ordinary phones, with big phone carriers as partners. SpaceX is building the same.
One of a handful of companies NASA pays to land on the Moon.
Takes pictures of the whole Earth every day with its own satellites; few do it at that scale.
Small rockets and Moon landers; strong rivals in both.
The only network that covers the whole globe on its frequencies, for ships, planes and the military.
Parts and systems for spacecraft; many suppliers do similar work.
Fast satellite pictures for governments; several rivals.
Runs the satellites behind iPhone emergency texts; much depends on Apple.
Satellite internet for planes and ships; losing ground to Starlink.
Space station and defense technology; a young company with rivals.
Makes parts for missiles and rockets that few suppliers can make.
Small satellites that collect weather and ship data; a small company in a crowded field.

themes.name: AI
themes.why: The companies building artificial intelligence: the software, chip designs, networks, power and servers behind it.

companies.note: Software governments and big companies use to run AI on their own data; hard to replace once in.
Its chip designs are in nearly every phone and growing in data centers; it earns a fee on each chip.
Fast network switches for AI data centers; Cisco and Nvidia compete.
Power and cooling for data centers; AI chips run hot, so demand grew.
Builds AI servers; Dell and others sell similar machines. Has had accounting troubles.
Rents out AI chips in the cloud; the big cloud companies compete, and it carries a lot of debt.
Servers and PCs; AI servers are its growth, with close rivals.

themes.name: Chips
themes.why: The chips inside every phone, computer and AI data center, and the machines that make them.

companies.note: Makes most AI chips, and its software keeps developers with it.
Custom AI chips for Google and others, plus network chips.
Makes the most advanced chips for almost everyone, Apple and Nvidia included.
The main rival to Intel in computer chips and to Nvidia in AI chips.
The only maker of the machines needed for the most advanced chips.
Phone chips and modem patents; Apple is moving to its own modem.
Memory chips; three big makers, and prices swing with supply.

themes.name: Software
themes.why: Business software and cybersecurity: once a company runs on it, it rarely leaves.

companies.note: The biggest sales and customer software; hard to leave once a company runs on it.
Workflow software big companies run their IT and HR on.
Photoshop and PDF, the standard for designers, though AI tools bring new rivals.
Cloud data storage and analysis; Databricks and the big clouds compete.
Watches companies' apps and servers for problems; many rivals.
Runs a huge network that makes websites fast and safe; few have one as big.
One of the largest cybersecurity companies; customers buy many products from it.
A leader in protecting company computers from hackers.
The online store platform behind millions of shops outside Amazon.
Software for writing and shipping code; Microsoft's GitHub is much bigger.
TurboTax and QuickBooks; most US small firms and filers use it.
A popular database; the cloud giants offer similar ones.

themes.name: Energy
themes.why: Oil, gas and the companies that drill for them. Results follow oil prices more than anything else.

companies.note: The largest US oil company; oil prices decide most of its results.
A big oil company; results follow oil prices.
Pumps oil and gas; results follow prices.
A US shale oil producer; results follow prices.
The largest oilfield services company; few can match its reach.
Owns many of the world's deepest-water drilling rigs; few rivals can drill there, but it carries a lot of debt.
